title: Small foreign body in the eye (dust, eyelash, grit)
summary: A loose speck of dust or eyelash on the surface of the eye is usually easy to flush out. Anything embedded, sharp, or stuck under the eyelid needs medical care.
steps: Tell the person not to rub the eye — that can scratch the cornea.
Sit them facing a strong light. Look carefully: ask them to look up, down, left, right.
If you can see a loose speck on the white of the eye or in the corner, try to flush it out with clean cool water poured gently from the inner corner outward.
If a speck is on the inside of the lower lid, pull the lid gently down and dab it out with the damp corner of a clean tissue.
If you cannot see the object easily or it does not flush out, cover the eye loosely with a clean dressing and arrange medical care.
avoid: Do not rub the eye, even if it itches.
Do not try to remove anything stuck on the coloured part of the eye, embedded in the white, or under the upper lid — go to a doctor.
Do not use cotton wool, tissues with loose fibres, or tweezers near the eye.
Do not apply eye drops, ointments, or home remedies without a doctor's advice.
whenToEscalate: Object stuck or embedded in the eye — emergency, do not try to remove it.
Pain, redness, watering, or blurred vision continues after the object has gone.
A high-speed injury — for example metal grinding, hammering, or an explosion — even if the eye looks normal.
Bleeding from the eye, change in pupil size or shape, or sensitivity to light.
Anyone who works with chemicals or metal who has eye pain — needs prompt review.
specialty: Eye casualty / ophthalmology; emergency department for embedded or high-speed injuries.
